data.name: Asgaroon
data.gender_notes: Asgaroon is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A warrior name derived from the Arabic word 'Asghar' meaning 'lion'. The name Asgaroon carries the meaning “Lion” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Pashto. Parents who choose Asgaroon usually hope their child will grow to embody lion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Protector, defender, and warrior in the service of God.
data.etymology: Asgaroon belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Asgaroon total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_urdu.name: اصغرون
in_urdu.long_meaning: اصغر سنی یا عمر کا حامل، یہ نام عربی جڑ سے ماخوذ ہے جو چھوٹی عمر یا لڑکپن کی طرف اشارہ کرتا ہے، اسلامی روایت میں بچوں یا نوجوانوں کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے

data.cultural_impact: The name 'Asgaroon' is considered to be a powerful, majestic, and regal name in Islamic culture due to its derivation from the fierce and dominant 'Asghar' meaning 'lion'. In various Islamic societies, naming a child this name would signify strength, courage, and nobility. It may also reflect the individual's desire to embody the qualities of a fearless warrior.
data.spiritual_significance: The name 'Asgaroon' holds a deeper spiritual meaning for Muslims who believe in the concept of Jihad or struggle in the way of God. The name is a reminder of the inner lion that every believer possesses, promoting resilience and perseverance during difficult times. It encourages individuals to confront their inner fears andifyahz their spiritual strength, reflecting the Quranic verse which says, 'And fight in the way of Allah and know that Allah hears and knows all things' (Quran 22:78). Ultimately, the name 'Asgaroon' symbolizes the warrior spirit within every believer and serves as a constant reminder of the power and strength available to them.
data.spiritual_symbolism: As-Sagaroon: The Sea Carriers. These namesakes are inspired by Prophet Sulaiman (Solomon), who was blessed with the ability to command the mighty winds and the seas. As-Sagaroon symbolizes the power and might of Allah, carried out by His chosen leaders.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Asgharoon were a prominent Sufi order in the Indian subcontinent during the medieval period. They were named after their founder, Shaikh Asghar Wali, who is believed to have lived during the late 12th or early 13th century.

The Asgharoon Sufi order gained significant popularity during the Mughal Empire in the 16th and 17th centuries. They were particularly known for their focus on the remembrance of Allah through music and dance, and were patronized by several Mughal emperors, including Akbar and Shah Jahan.
historical_references.context: Mughal Empire, Sufi order, Music and dance

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Asgaroon' is derived from the Islamic tradition and is associated with the legendary hero, Al-Asghar ibn Ali, who is considered one of the holy figures in Shia Islam. Despite being a historical figure, the name 'Asgaroon' is still relevant in modern times and is seen on various digital platforms. On Twitter, users often use the hashtag #Asgaroon to discuss and share information related to Islamic history, art and culture, and spiritual and religious practices. Instagram is another popular platform where users share images and videos inspired by the life and teachings of Al-Asghar ibn Ali, using the tag #Asgaroon or #AlAsghar. On YouTube, there are several channels dedicated to the study and promotion of Asgaroon's teachings, including educational videos, spiritual talks, and animated stories for children.
